narrativeReportMd:
# EnrollmentResponse R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local R4-valid `EnrollmentResponse` instance pattern was found that becomes invalid solely because of a local R6 cardinality, type, modifier, reference-target, or required-code removal. The main risks are migration and runtime risks: R6 adds `EnrollmentResponse.candidate`, which has no native R4 location, and changes `EnrollmentResponse.outcome` from the shared remittance outcome binding to an enrollment-specific required binding.

## Scope
The comparison used the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, manifest row, and directly relevant terminology artifacts. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and `Extension` changes are excluded from findings and listed out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Existing local elements are mostly stable. R4 systems moving forward to R6 should not need to populate new mandatory data, because `candidate` is optional. R6 systems moving data backward to R4 need a policy for preserving `candidate`, usually an extension, profile-specific rule, or lossy omission. Terminology-aware implementations should update `outcome` validation and generated enum metadata from `remittance-outcome` to `enrollment-outcome`, even though the package code lists currently contain the same four lexical codes.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is the R6-to-R4 representability gap for `candidate`; dropping it can lose the subject or group intended to be enrolled. The `outcome` binding change is lower at the instance JSON level but important for validators, generated code, terminology services, and business rules that key off canonical ValueSet or CodeSystem URLs.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the `outcome` binding change because the supplied packages do not include an official ConceptMap or narrative rationale for replacing the remittance binding with an enrollment-specific binding.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 `candidate` addition is a relatively compatible forward change because it is optional. The `outcome` canonical replacement could have been softened by retaining the old ValueSet canonical as an alias, publishing a ConceptMap, or using a broader shared ValueSet with an enrollment-specific binding name.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes and EnrollmentResponse SearchParameter changes should be assessed by their own reports. Terminology analysis should confirm official expansions and any intended cross-version mapping for `remittance-outcome` to `enrollment-outcome`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for `EnrollmentResponse`. The top migration concerns are R6-only `candidate`, the `outcome` required-binding canonical change, and terminology/codegen updates around financial workflow enums. The main uncertainty is the lack of an official diff or ConceptMap explaining the outcome binding replacement.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The local resource model is additive rather than subtractive: R6 preserves the R4 local elements and adds optional `candidate`. Forward migration from R4 therefore has low validation risk, while backward migration from R6 has a meaningful data-preservation risk if `candidate` is populated. Terminology migration should focus on canonical URLs and generated enum names rather than lexical code transforms, because the complete local CodeSystems compared here have the same `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial` codes for the old and new outcome bindings.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural element, cardinality, type, reference-target, flag, and local constraint comparisons because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for the semantic intent of the `outcome` binding replacement because no official cross-version diff, narrative rationale, terminology expansion, or ConceptMap was supplied.

findings.title: R6 adds optional EnrollmentResponse.candidate with no native R4 equivalent

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 snapshot and differential end the local content model at `requestProvider`; there is no local element for the patient or group being enrolled.

newState.summary: R6 adds `candidate` as an optional reference to Patient or Group.

semanticText.definition: The subject or group of subjects to be enrolled.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a direct, optional slot for the enrollment candidate. The element is local to `EnrollmentResponse`, not inherited from a base resource.

facts.newValue: No native R4 element can carry this candidate reference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `candidate` is a new R6 element id and path with no same-name or semantically equivalent local element in the R4 `EnrollmentResponse` StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `candidate` is optional, an R4 instance remains validly representable in R6 without adding it. The breaking pressure is in the opposite direction: an R6 instance that uses `candidate` cannot be represented in base R4 without an extension or lossy omission, and a strict R4 validator will reject the unknown `candidate` property. Runtime risk is medium for parsers, generated R4 models, and mapping code that assume every EnrollmentResponse field has an R4 property.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing the subject or group intended to be enrolled can affect enrollment workflow reconciliation and downstream payer/member business logic, even though the resource itself is financial rather than direct clinical care.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent the subject or group of subjects being enrolled directly on the enrollment response.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; `candidate` is an optional R6 addition that does not invalidate R4 EnrollmentResponse instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional `EnrollmentResponse.candidate` is a reasonable way to close the base-model gap for identifying the patient or group being enrolled. The change does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6, because the new element has cardinality `0..1`. The remaining incompatibility is an R6-to-R4 representability issue when new R6 data is populated, which is expected for genuinely new optional content rather than evidence that the R6 base design was unnecessarily breaking.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue: existing R4 instances can migrate without adding `candidate`. A cross-version extension or profile rule could preserve `candidate` during R6-to-R4 downgrade, but that is a migration/backport mitigation rather than a less-breaking base R6 design. The only base-design alternative that fully avoids the downgrade gap is not adding the element, which would leave the subject/group modeling goal unmet.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or downgrade mappings are migration mitigations, not less-breaking R6 base designs; omitting `candidate` would fail the R6 modeling goal.

evidence.detail: No R4 snapshot element with id `EnrollmentResponse.candidate` exists.
R6 defines `candidate` with min 0, max 1, and type Reference(Patient|Group).
evidence.quote: The subject or group of subjects to be enrolled.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is illustrative of the representability issue. The extension URL in the migration example is a placeholder; a real migration should use an agreed cross-version extension or implementation-guide rule.

findings.narrativeMd: `EnrollmentResponse.candidate` is a new optional R6 element for the patient or group being enrolled. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because old instances can omit it, but it is material for round-trip and downgrade workflows. An R6 response that includes the candidate carries business-critical subject context that base R4 has no native place to store.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances do not become invalid merely because `candidate` was added. R6 instances containing `candidate` are not valid base R4 instances and will be rejected by strict R4 validation as containing an unknown element. A lossy R6-to-R4 transform could drop the element, but that changes business semantics and prevents lossless round-trip.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, no backfill is required unless local policy wants candidate populated. For R6-to-R4 migration, define a cross-version extension or profile-specific mapping for `candidate`, and test downgrade/upgrade round trips for both Patient and Group references. If omission is allowed, make the data loss explicit in mapping documentation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The optional addition was a relatively compatible way to improve the base model. The remaining incompatibility is unavoidable once base R6 exposes information that base R4 lacks. A standard extension could have provided better cross-version compatibility, but at the cost of weaker base-model visibility.

findings.title: EnrollmentResponse.outcome required binding changed from remittance-outcome to enrollment-outcome

oldState.summary: R4 `outcome` is a code with required binding to `ValueSet/remittance-outcome|4.0.1`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet composes all codes from the complete `http://hl7.org/fhir/remittance-outcome` CodeSystem. The local CodeSystem contains `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses the shared remittance outcome terminology for EnrollmentResponse outcome values.

newState.summary: R6 `outcome` remains a code with required binding, but the binding is now `ValueSet/enrollment-outcome|6.0.0-ballot4`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet composes all codes from the complete `http://hl7.org/fhir/enrollment-outcome` CodeSystem. The local CodeSystem contains the same lexical codes as the R4 remittance outcome CodeSystem: `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 switches to an enrollment-specific terminology canonical while keeping the same element name, cardinality, primitive type, and displayed code list.

facts.note: The local complete CodeSystems have the same four code strings, though under different canonical CodeSystem URLs.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path and id are unchanged (`EnrollmentResponse.outcome`); only the required terminology binding canonical and binding name changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR `code` elements serialize only the code string, and the compared complete CodeSystems expose the same four code strings. Therefore a typical instance with `outcome: "complete"` remains lexically valid in both versions. The risk is nevertheless material for generated enums, validators, terminology services, rule engines, and conformance tests that identify the binding by ValueSet or CodeSystem canonical URL rather than by code string alone.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The changed canonical can cause processing or validation disagreement, but the code meanings visible in the local packages appear aligned and the element is financial workflow status rather than a direct clinical safety field.

justification.inferredGoal: Move EnrollmentResponse outcome away from a remittance-specific terminology to an enrollment-specific terminology.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `remittance-outcome` required binding while clarifying enrollment semantics, or introduce `enrollment-outcome` only as a secondary/additional binding during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--using enrollment-specific terminology for an EnrollmentResponse outcome--is reasonable, and the instance-level break is limited because both local code systems contain the same four code strings. However, replacing the required ValueSet and CodeSystem canonicals is still disruptive for terminology-aware validators, generated enums, caches, and conformance tests. A less-breaking path exists, but it would not cleanly achieve the domain-specific canonical identity and could create long-lived ambiguity, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `ValueSet/remittance-outcome` as the required binding for R6 while updating descriptions and binding metadata to document its use for enrollment outcomes, possibly with `ValueSet/enrollment-outcome` as an additional or transitional binding. That would preserve most R4 tooling assumptions and avoid canonical replacement for the unchanged lexical code set. Its material tradeoff is that the base resource would continue to expose a remittance-oriented canonical for enrollment semantics, and maintaining two same-code terminology identities could confuse validation, code generation, and future code-set evolution.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would reduce canonical-URL churn but preserve a misleading remittance-named primary terminology and risk dual terminology identities if the value sets later diverge.

evidence.detail: R4 required binding is `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/remittance-outcome|4.0.1` with binding name `RemittanceOutcome`.
R6 required binding is `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/enrollment-outcome|6.0.0-ballot4` with binding name `EnrollmentOutcome`.
R4 remittance-outcome complete CodeSystem contains `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`.
R6 enrollment-outcome complete CodeSystem contains `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`.
No local ConceptMap was found mapping `remittance-outcome` to `enrollment-outcome`.

examples.examplesMd: The serialized instance code usually does not change; the migration work is updating terminology canonical references, generated enum names, validation bindings, and documentation.

findings.narrativeMd: `EnrollmentResponse.outcome` keeps the same path, cardinality, and `code` type, but its required ValueSet changes from the R4 remittance outcome canonical to an R6 enrollment outcome canonical. This is easy to miss because the displayed code list remains `queued | complete | error | partial`. Implementations that treat the binding canonical as part of generated model or validation identity can still break even when instance JSON strings do not change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A simple R4 instance with `outcome` equal to one of the four compared codes should not become invalid in R6 on code value alone. However, validation harnesses pinned to the old ValueSet URL, terminology caches, generated enums named after `RemittanceOutcome`, or business rules that check the old CodeSystem URL may fail or require reconfiguration. R6-to-R4 representability risk is low for bare JSON instances because the same lexical code strings are present in the R4 CodeSystem.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update terminology configuration from `ValueSet/remittance-outcome|4.0.1` to `ValueSet/enrollment-outcome|6.0.0-ballot4` for R6. Regenerate code and enum bindings if they use ValueSet or CodeSystem canonical URLs. Add regression tests for all four code strings and for terminology-service validation using both old and new ValueSet URLs. If downgrading R6 to R4, map the same code string but document that the binding canonical changes back to remittance outcome.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change appears aimed at better domain specificity, but canonical replacement is more disruptive than a pure description or binding-name update. A compatible transition would publish an explicit ConceptMap or alias and preserve the old binding as an additional or legacy-compatible binding where tooling can discover it.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology equivalence is based on local complete CodeSystem concept lists, not on an official expansion or ConceptMap. Human review should confirm whether the R6 `enrollment-outcome` CodeSystem intentionally inherits the R4 remittance semantics.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The resource keeps the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag. Governance metadata changed and is captured as a notable non-breaking change.
No local R4 elements were removed or renamed. The only local presence change found is the R6 addition of `candidate`, which is reported as a finding.
For local elements present in both versions, min and max cardinalities are unchanged.
For local elements present in both versions, primitive/datatype/reference type codes are unchanged.
`request`, `organization`, and `requestProvider` retain their R4 target profiles. The target profiles on new `candidate` are covered by the added-element finding.
No local EnrollmentResponse-specific invariants were added, removed, or strengthened. Inherited base-resource constraint expression changes are out of scope.
No local fixed values, pattern values, or default values were found on EnrollmentResponse elements in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were found or changed.
The local `status` element remains a modifier in both versions with the same modifier reason. No other local modifier flag changes were found.
The local `status` summary flag remains true and other shared local elements remain non-summary. Inherited `modifierExtension` summary behavior is out of scope.
No local slicing definitions were found on EnrollmentResponse in either version.

The resourceType and existing local JSON property names are stable. Serialization/codegen impact is limited to the new `candidate` property and terminology-binding metadata for `outcome`, both reported as findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Status binding version updated to fm-status 6.0.0-ballot4 with unchanged local code set
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `status` remains a `0..1` `code` with required binding to `ValueSet/fm-status`; only the version suffix changes from `4.0.1` to `6.0.0-ballot4`. The complete local R4 and R6 `fm-status` CodeSystems both contain `active`, `cancelled`, `draft`, and `entered-in-error` with the same definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology caches and generated enum metadata should be refreshed for the R6 package version, but no instance value transform is indicated by the local package contents.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact governance status changed from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The StructureDefinition status changes from `draft` to `active`, and the standards-status extension changes from `trial-use` to `normative`, while the resource identity and local content model are retained. This affects conformance expectations and maturity signaling, not instance serialization.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat R6 EnrollmentResponse as more stable and may tighten governance around deviations, but existing instances are not invalidated by this metadata change alone.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records `mustSupport: false` on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omits `mustSupport` on the compared local elements while R6 explicitly includes `mustSupport: false`. Because the effective value is not strengthened to true, this does not create a new support obligation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or diff tools should normalize absent and false `mustSupport` values to avoid noisy false-positive changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited `Resource` element changes such as `language` binding strength/version changes and `implicitRules` text changes appear in the snapshot but are excluded from this local EnrollmentResponse report.

The `outcome` binding canonical changed from `remittance-outcome` to `enrollment-outcome`; a terminology-focused review should confirm official expansions and any intended ConceptMap.
R6 adds search parameters that appear to expose the new `candidate` element, but SearchParameter changes are outside this StructureDefinition report.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review an official HL7 change log, ballot reconciliation note, or rendered diff for EnrollmentResponse.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local ConceptMap was found between R4 `remittance-outcome` and R6 `enrollment-outcome`, limiting certainty about intended semantic equivalence beyond matching lexical codes and similar definitions.
